payload.analysis: Combined with the suspicion of congenital hereditary keratoderma, genetic testing identified a heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant, and parental testing showed absence in both parents, confirming a de novo mutation. This establishes pachyonychia congenita, consistent with nail, skin, and oral mucosal findings. Lack of family history is explained by de novo occurrence. All key genetic information is covered; skin biopsy was not obtained but is not essential given molecular confirmation.

why.why: Genetic testing identified a heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant that is absent in both parents, confirming a de novo mutation diagnostic of Pachyonychia congenita, a congenital hereditary keratoderma. The clinical triad of nail dystrophy, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, and oral leukokeratosis matches this diagnosis. Pathologist and laboratory physician analyses agree that molecular confirmation is sufficient even without skin biopsy, so confidence rises from 0.75 to 0.98.

payload.analysis: Combining the clinical triad of nail dystrophy, palmoplantar keratoderma, and oral leukokeratosis with the heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del variant confirmed by whole-exome sequencing and Sanger validation, and its absence in both parents indicating a de novo mutation, the diagnosis of Pachyonychia congenita is established. This molecular finding refutes chronic inflammatory dermatosis and congenital ectodermal dysplasia. All key genetic and clinical information is covered.

payload.report: Clinical triad (nail dystrophy, palmoplantar hyperkeratosis, oral leukokeratosis) indicated congenital hereditary keratoderma. Heterozygous KRT6A c.1460-2_1460del absent in both parents confirms a de novo mutation; whole-exome/Sanger validation and expert opinion deemed molecular evidence sufficient. Normal hair, teeth, intelligence, and absent family history support this. In the graph, node-11 refines node-6 to Pachyonychia congenita due to de novo KRT6A mutation, making the frontier sufficiently specific; ectodermal dysplasia and chronic inflammatory dermatosis are refuted. Diagnosis: Pachyonychia congenita caused by de novo KRT6A mutation.
